q1: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT CLASS, COUNT(STUDENT) AS NO_STUDENTS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS) AS TEMP WHERE NO_STUDENTS >=5
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT CLASS, COUNT(STUDENT) AS NO_STUDENTS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS) AS TEMP WHERE NO_STUDENTS >=5
explanation: Both queries aim to find classes that have at least 5 students enrolled. Q1 directly groups by CLASS and filters where the count of students is greater than or equal to 5. Q2 achieves the same by first grouping by CLASS and counting students, then filtering in the outer SELECT where the count is greater than or equal to 5. The logic and the end result are the same.
